summary.text: A 14-year-old boy attended the neurology outpatient department with sudden, gradually progressive bilateral blurring of vision, dizziness and head rolling for 10 days, and weakness of the right upper limb for two days. He had recovered from typhoid three months earlier and had no history of falls, trauma or diabetes.

Examination showed visual acuity 14/24 and 6/12, a Snellen chart reading of 22/32, Ishihara 6/17 in the right and 8/17 in the left eye, a right-eye strabismus, reduced right upper limb strength of 3/5 and normal reflexes. MRI showed STIR hyperintensity with mild contrast enhancement of the posterior bilateral optic nerves extending to the chiasm in optic neuritis, and he was referred to neurophysiotherapy.

He was admitted to AVBRH and physiotherapy started on 18/10/2023: patient education, gaze stability, eye-hand coordination, eyeball resistance, habituation and Cawthorne-Cooksey exercises and right upper limb strengthening with a 1 litre water bottle; the rehabilitation consisted of six weeks and a post-rehabilitation MRI was obtained. The exercises helped his coordination and quality of life; the Functional Independence Measure rose from 50 to 110 and the NEI Visual Functioning Questionnaire-25 from 40 to 90.
